sourceDateMeaning: Official pages were accessed and reviewed on this date; vendor publication or update dates are recorded only when directly available.

claims.scope: Official Bolt (bolt.new by StackBlitz) GitHub workflow for project source backup and synchronization; requires an authorized GitHub account and repository access.
claims.value: Bolt documents connecting an existing GitHub repository or creating a new one, automatic code synchronization, project history outside Bolt, and branch-based workflows. The same code can be worked on in GitHub and returned to Bolt.
claims.limitation: This documents code and repository handoff only. It does not establish transfer of Bolt Cloud data, secrets, domains, integrations, deployment settings, or a tested complete project migration.

claims.scope: Official Bolt project publishing through Bolt Hosting, including the published web address; excludes account-specific bandwidth and paid feature entitlements.
claims.value: Bolt documents built-in hosting and publishing to a live URL with a free bolt.host subdomain without requiring a separate hosting account. Its official Netlify documentation also describes an alternative external deployment path, subject to connection and project-state prerequisites.
claims.limitation: The public workflow does not prove that every app can be moved unchanged to another host or that runtime behavior, databases, secrets, domains, and operational settings migrate with the source code. Current hosting limits and paid features require checking the applicable plan.

claims.scope: Documented options for using Bolt Database or Supabase as an app backend, including the official database-claim/connect workflow; not a test of an actual migration.
claims.value: Bolt documents a built-in database by default and, on Pro and Teams plans, options to claim a Bolt Database in Supabase or connect an existing Supabase database. The docs say switching from Bolt Database to Supabase later requires extra steps and recommend choosing the backend early.
claims.limitation: This is not evidence of a complete, one-click, lossless export of database contents, files, users, secrets, functions, domains, and deployment configuration. No real account, export, restore, or migration was performed; plan eligibility and project-specific steps must be checked.

claims.scope: Integrations explicitly listed in Bolt's public product documentation; does not claim an exhaustive connector catalog or uniform plan availability.
claims.value: Bolt's official overview lists Expo for mobile apps, Stripe for payments, GitHub for source control, Google SSO, MCP servers, and Bolt Cloud databases, hosting, and domains. Separate official docs describe Netlify and Supabase paths.
claims.limitation: Integration behavior can require external accounts, credentials, permissions, or paid plans. The overview does not establish that all integrations work for every project, account, region, or plan, or that connected resources are portable.

claims.scope: Public Bolt plan and usage display observed on the review date; does not represent individualized checkout, taxes, external provider charges, or an app's total operating cost.
claims.value: The public pricing page displayed Free at $0 with a 300,000-token daily limit and 1 million-token monthly limit, Pro at $25 per month billed monthly, and Teams at $30 per member per month billed monthly. It describes hosting and request allowances separately from AI tokens.
claims.limitation: Prices, annual-versus-monthly billing, eligibility, region, taxes, promotions, and account entitlements may vary or change. Token use depends on project size and work; hosting, database, domain, and third-party costs are not represented by the subscription price. Confirm current checkout and service usage before estimating cost.

claims.scope: Publicly documented project security checks and customer follow-up actions; not a complete service-level, support, or customer-operations contract.
claims.value: Bolt documents project security audits and database checks, recommends a security check before publishing, and notes that some findings require the project owner to change settings in connected services. This indicates that platform checks do not remove all customer-side review and operations work.
claims.limitation: The documentation does not establish that scans guarantee security or assign a particular customer's ongoing responsibility for incident response, backups, dependency upgrades, monitoring, recovery objectives, or support coverage. No project was audited for this snapshot.

claims.scope: Official Git sync and code download options for Lovable projects; repository permissions, provider connections, and plan-specific download access apply.
claims.value: Lovable documents automatic two-way code sync with GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket, plus code download for a copy. The repository can be cloned and edited locally, and synced code can be deployed outside Lovable. A repository contains code and migration files, not the database contents.
claims.limitation: Git sync does not transfer all runtime services or credentials. The docs specifically exclude database contents, Lovable-managed connector credentials, secrets, and some backend actions from a simple source handoff; pushing code does not itself publish the live site or run every migration/function deployment.

claims.scope: Official publishing and hosting behavior for a Lovable project, including public URL and custom-domain plan boundaries.
claims.value: Lovable documents publishing a project snapshot to a lovable.app URL with HTTPS; custom domains and branded workspace domains have plan-specific availability. Code changes do not affect the live snapshot until the user publishes again.
claims.limitation: This documents Lovable hosting, not a tested deployment to another provider or equivalent portability of Cloud, authentication, storage, secrets, connectors, domains, and operational configuration. Hosting usage can incur credits based on the app's runtime activity.

claims.scope: Official Lovable Cloud database export and documented migration boundaries; excludes a claim that a complete environment has been migrated successfully.
claims.value: Lovable documents exporting Cloud database structure and data and describes a migration path that separately moves code, restores or rebuilds against a destination backend, and reconfigures required services. The database export excludes storage files, Edge Function code, and secrets; sign-in provider settings and project API keys are also configured separately at the destination.
claims.limitation: The documented export has size, availability, and frequency limits, and a backend move requires separate configuration and validation. No actual account export, restore, authentication cutover, or end-to-end migration was tested. Do not describe this as turnkey portability.

claims.scope: Officially documented Lovable connector types and direct/custom API integration patterns; exact connector availability, permissions, and charges vary.
claims.value: Lovable documents app-plus-chat connectors, personal chat/MCP connectors, app-user connectors, custom connectors, and direct API integrations. Managed connectors can keep credentials outside app code; direct integrations place credential and request handling within the app's configured secrets/server-side path.
claims.limitation: A connector category does not prove a specific service is available on every plan or for every workspace. OAuth scopes, workspace roles, external provider limits, credentials, and third-party costs vary; no integration was connected or tested for this snapshot.

claims.scope: Public credit charging and usage-specific grant rules; excludes individualized checkout, current workspace migration state, and a fixed total cost for an app.
claims.value: Lovable documents credits across build/chat and runtime categories including Cloud, AI Gateway, and connectors, with different usage-specific grants, refresh periods, and expiry rules. Its docs caution that grants and chat pricing can change; project runtime usage and credit rates depend on feature, plan, and account.
claims.limitation: A plan subscription is not a fixed total cost for building and running an app. This review did not inspect a specific account or checkout. Confirm the workspace's current balance, usage details, plan, provider charges, and current terms.

claims.scope: Lovable's published security-analysis boundaries and the app builder/customer responsibilities stated in its official documentation.
claims.value: Lovable documents automated security scans and states that users remain responsible for ensuring their apps meet use-case security requirements; scans do not guarantee complete security and do not replace a thorough or professional review for sensitive or critical apps.
claims.limitation: This does not define every customer's staffing, incident-response plan, backup/restore testing, dependency operations, monitoring, recovery objective, support entitlement, or contractual allocation. No generated app or workspace was audited for this snapshot.
